title: Ukraine's citation base is 3.29% of ref cells - and Length [ref] and Capacity [ref] are each filled on exactly ONE of 47 rows
summary: 34 of 1,034 [ref] cells are filled (3.29%) against 18.49% tracker-wide, and of the 22 refs on operating rows 17 are dead links. The distribution is the finding: Route [ref] 8 rows, Status [ref] 7, Diameter [ref] 5, Fuel [ref] 4, PipelineType [ref] 4, Construction [ref] 2, Start [ref] 2, Capacity [ref] 1, Length [ref] 1, every other ref column 0. Length and capacity are exactly what this pass found wrong, repeatedly and independently - 292.00 km unsourced on both Ivatsevychi rows against sourced 357.7/366.7 km strings, 29.00 bcm/y restated on both as a system total, P0784's 24.00 bcm/y verbatim an aggregate over three threads, P1481's 333.00 km unable to span its own ~424 km corridor, and neither KZU length supported by anything. The cells the country cannot cite are the cells it gets wrong. CORRECTION TO THIS PASS'S OWN EARLIER WORDING: an intermediate draft called Ukraine 'the worst-cited scope in the tracker'. It is 2nd of 52 country scopes with 20+ gas rows, behind the Netherlands (3.03%, n=39) and effectively tied with Bangladesh (3.30%, n=62), ahead of Indonesia (4.27%) and Thailand (4.28%) - so the useful escalation is that there is a BOTTOM-TIER COHORT of five unswept scopes at 3-4% covering ~230 gas rows, of which Ukraine is the first to get a section-9 pass. Calibration for the next one: a blank cell in Ukraine is evidence nobody looked, NOT evidence the fact is unpublished - do not import Kazakhstan's tolerance for UNRESOLVED. Two access facts, both BLOCKS not deletions: utg.ua and tsoua.com return HTTP 403 (operator WAF) and between them hold the Ukrtransgaz chronology that would settle clusters A and C - read via Wayback; moldovatransgaz.md fails TLS and the mtg.md mirror is what this pass staged.

title: Owner: three cells record [100.%] alongside a second named owner, and six put a sole non-Ukrainian owner on a row that lists Ukraine
summary: READ THE NARROW VERSION. Gazprom appears in Owner on 20 of the 47 rows, but for 14 of them the unweighted pair 'Gazprom PJSC; Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' on a genuinely transnational Russia+Ukraine row is the DEFENSIBLE convention, not a defect - so this pass's earlier reading that P0783 is an instance is WITHDRAWN. Two narrow classes survive. (1) A percentage of [100.%] recorded alongside a second named owner, arithmetically impossible and NOT Gazprom-specific: P0768 and P0776 put Gazprom at 100% beside GTSOU, and P0761 puts GTSOU at 100% beside Gazprom AND QazaqGaz. This is a NOTATION question only Baird can settle - if [100.%] means '100% of the section in that party's own country' the convention needs writing into gem_schema.md because it does not read that way; if it means a share of the whole line, all three cells are wrong. A researcher cannot source which GEM means. (2) A sole non-Ukrainian owner on a row listing Ukraine: P0791 (Gazprom; QazaqGaz), P0793, P1471, P2387 and P1485 (all Gazprom PJSC [100.%]), plus P5935 (Moldovatransgaz [100.%]) - the last of which argues this is a convention gap rather than a bias. P1485 is the unambiguous one and the row to fix first: its CountriesOrAreas is 'Ukraine' ALONE, a 532 km wholly-Ukrainian operating line recorded as 100% Gazprom-owned, when the 1 January 2020 unbundling put the transmission system under Gas TSO of Ukraine LLC. Also flagged: P1487 still names Ukrtransgaz, the pre-2020 entity. STAGED as row-level attribution concerns: P1485 (cluster C), P0775 and P0776 (cluster H). MEMO-ONLY, no row action exists: the class-1 notation question, the other five class-2 rows, and P1487's stale name.

title: GulfPub: all three escalation gates crossed - 85 additions, 23 discovery candidates, 20.5% status conflicts - and the conflicts collapse to 5 GEM rows with two one-to-many attractors
summary: 158 reference records, 73 overlaps (46.2% - a healthy run, name axis 100% named, both sides 100% routed, no MATCH_QUALITY warning), 85 additions, 17 gem_only. The 23 DISCOVERY_CANDIDATEs are the substantive half and are NOT stubs: named Ukrainian trunk lines at 25-170 km that GEM does not carry - Chernihiv-Boyarka 170.6, Stryi-Kolomyia 128.0, Voloske-Zhovti Vody 123.4, Berezovka-Ilyichevsk 108.6, Dolina-Lviv 99.2 (twice), Starodub-Shostka 90.9, Rivne-Sarny 84.6, Novoodeskyi-Ochakov 74.5, Chernivtsi-Kolomyia 74.7 and more - plus a Crimean offshore-storage cluster (Golitsynskoe-Glebovskoe 107.4, Shtormovoe-Glebovskoe 115.9, Dzhanoy-Simferopol 90.2, Strelkovoe-Dzhankoy 47.7) and White Stream (idle, 1,392.7 km, a known Black Sea proposal - check whether GEM carries it under another scope before treating it as missing). Over the 5-cluster Discovery gate several times over; each needs matching to an existing GEM row under another name (-> OtherEnglishNames) BEFORE any Discovery staging. ON THE STATUS CONFLICTS, do not read 15/73 = 20.5% at face value: they collapse to FIVE GEM rows, and two of those are one-to-many ATTRACTOR matches rather than disagreements - P1487 (Poland-Ukraine Interconnector, cancelled) is matched to five unrelated GulfPub operating lines including Komsomolsk-Radushnoe and Radushnoe-Maryevka, which are nowhere near a Poland interconnector, and P0788 (Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka) is matched to five as well. What remains genuinely live is three questions: P0761 Soyuz mothballed vs GulfPub operating, P0788 Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka mothballed vs operating (behind the bad matches), and - directly relevant to redundancy cluster E - P7817 construction and P7818 proposed against GulfPub operating on Slavyansk-Taganrog, Kushchevskaya-Mariupol and Mariupol-Berdyansk. P0791's operating-vs-proposed pair is a mismatch to a differently-named line. Do not auto-flip any of them.

title: OSM: 1,003 additions crosses the gate on volume alone - 81% of the extract is sub-kilometre fragments, and the operator tags show distribution networks GGIT does not track
summary: 1,004 reference records against 51 GEM rows, 1 overlap, 1,003 additions (298 FRAGMENT_OF_EXISTING, 702 DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE, 3 NEAR_MISS). Read the health line before reading the buckets: 100% of refs carry geometry, 100% of GEM rows are routed, escalations EMPTY - MATCH_QUALITY correctly did NOT fire, because neither axis is dead. The 0.1% overlap rate is a SCOPE mismatch, not a matcher defect. The median DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE is 0.05 km (50 metres) and 815 of 1,004 features are under 1 km; the named operator tags say what they are - Talnivske UEGG (78 features), Cherkasytransgaz (26), Kyivgaz (18) are district and city gas DISTRIBUTION utilities, which GGIT does not cover. Only 12 candidates reach 100 km and only 32 of the 702 carry a name at all. The genuinely worth-a-look subset is small: the two 'Krasnodar Krai - Crimea' traces (217.2 and 136.3 km, the Russian-built Crimea line) and 'Soyuz' (215.4 km), plus the three unnamed 300-429 km traces. REGISTRY-LEVEL FINDING, not a Ukraine one: the OSM extractor filters on man_made=pipeline + substance=gas and does NOT preserve usage or pressure, so no extract in the registry can separate transmission from distribution. Sub-kilometre fragments dominate everywhere (Iraq 84.6% under 1 km, Libya 66.7%, Egypt 52.4%, Kazakhstan 42.9%); Ukraine is not anomalous in KIND, only in VOLUME (1,004 features against a registry maximum of 112 elsewhere), because Ukrainian distribution networks are densely mapped in OSM. Consequence: the >30-additions gate is structurally uninformative for OSM and should not be read as a Discovery signal without a length or usage filter first. Recommended fix, NOT done here because it would invalidate seven countries' committed runs: preserve usage/pressure in the extractor so a transmission filter becomes possible. Logged to docs/research_backlog.md.

title: System-level values restated on strings - two confirmed instances, both already carried as row actions
summary: The motif India (107.00 MMSCMD on five HVJ rows) and Kazakhstan (six systems) both carry appears in Ukraine, but SMALLER than an early draft implied - a full-tab check finds only two genuine instances, and both are already staged as row-level cluster actions rather than needing separate handling. (1) P3484 and P5938 (Ivatsevychi-Kobryn-Dolyna I and II) are byte-identical on BOTH capacity and length: 29.00 bcm/y and 292.00 km each. GEM's own note says the 29.00 is the system total, ISANS 2023 puts the corridor near 30, and UTG's chronology gives the two strings as 357.7 km (1976) and 366.7 km (1977) - so summing the rows double-counts 29 bcm/y AND both lengths are wrong. That is redundancy cluster G, which REFUTED the duplicate while falsifying both numbers - a refuted duplicate is not a clean row. (2) P0784's 24.00 bcm/y is verbatim an aggregate over three threads in Moldovatransgaz's own table and double-counts capacity P0786 (23.70) already carries; that is cluster B. The only other repeated capacity in the scope, 8.00 bcm/y on P0778 and P1487, is coincidental - different corridors. 17 of the 47 rows carry no capacity at all.

title: A dead source came back: the archived VNIPItransgaz object table sources SEVEN of this scope's uncited length/diameter cells - and its rowspan'd name cells are a trap that already produced one wrong figure
summary: vtg.com.ua/experience/main/gts.html is a genuine live 404, and an earlier stage of this pass concluded from that the figures resting on it were 'unsourced, not merely unverified'. THAT IS WITHDRAWN. A Wayback capture of the VNIPItransgaz (Ukrainian gas-transmission design institute) "Osnovnye obyekty" table verifies 200 and serves the whole thing: https://web.archive.org/web/20220608014635/http://www.vtg.com.ua/experience/main/gts.html?lang=ru . Repointing a dead ref to its archived capture is standing practice here, and it matters more than usual in the worst-cited scope in the tracker's bottom tier - the table carries name, diameter, pressure, length, number of strings and countries for every Soviet-era trunk crossing Ukraine, and it is the single source behind seven ref units staged in this packet: P0793 (Stavropol-Moscow, 700/800 mm - the sheet's Diameter cell was BLANK - and 1262 km), P1471 (Novopskov-Aksai-Mozdok, 1200 mm and 878 km, both matching the sheet exactly), P1457 (Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov, 516 km), P5938 (Ivatsevichy-Dolyna, 1200 mm and a THIRD string GEM does not carry) and the cluster-A correction below. NOW THE TRAP, because it has already cost us one number. The table groups several lines under ONE system heading whose name cell carries a rowspan, listing the sub-line names inside that single cell; the sub-names map IN ORDER onto the data rows beneath. Read a row without checking its grouping and you attribute another line's spec to yours. That is exactly what produced P0777's 1,112.00 km: 522 km is Shebelinka-Dykanka-Kyiv and 590 km is Kyiv-Western Ukraine - two DIFFERENT lines in one block - so 1,112 is the KZU line plus the upstream trunk summed. This CONFIRMS the conflation cluster A had flagged as a question for the human, and turns it into a documented finding: the fix is a scope statement in ResearcherNotes next to the corrected value, not just a smaller number. The same block structure puts three separate lines (Stavropol-Moscow, Krasnodar Krai-Serpukhov, Novopskov-Aksai-Mozdok) under 'Severny Kavkaz-Tsentr' with a single countries cell reading 'Russia' - which is an aggregate imprecision, NOT evidence against Novopskov being in Ukraine (see P1471). One tension to record rather than resolve: VTG gives Kyiv-Western Ukraine as 590 km on one string against UTG's construction chronology 183.6 + 216.3 = 399.90 km on two. The operator's own chronology is the better source and 399.90 stands; the 590 belongs in ResearcherNotes as a documented second-source disagreement.
